paper.title: High-Dimensional Dynamic Pricing Under Nonstationarity: Learning and Earning with Change-Point Detection

settings.name_in_paper: High-dimensional dynamic pricing under non-stationarity (piecewise-stationary high-dimensional GLM demand)
unmapped: Action is a scalar price p_t in [p_l,p_u]; demand y_t follows a GLM in x_t=(z_t,p_t) with parameter theta_t in R^d, revenue p_t*psi'(z_t'alpha_t+beta_t p_t)

Parameter theta_t is s-sparse with ||theta_t||_1 <= C_theta; covariates entry-wise bounded, i.i.d. within each stationary segment with (2+delta)-moment and min-eigenvalue conditions (distribution may change across segments)
Number of change-points Upsilon_T (mapped to S_T) unknown to the learner; change sizes unknown
settings.definition_quote: we assume that there exist $\Upsilon_T$ unknown time periods $1\leq\tau_1<\tau_2<\cdots <\tau_{\Upsilon_T} <T$ such that $\theta_t \neq \theta_{t + 1}$ if and only if $t \in \{\tau_1, \ldots, \tau_{\Upsilon_T}\}$. ... $R_T^\pi(\bm \theta_T)= \sum_{k=0}^{\Upsilon_T}\sum_{t=\tau_{k}+1}^{\tau_{k+1}} \mathbb E\left\{ r(p_t^*,\theta_t,z_t)-r(p_t^\pi,\theta_t,z_t) \right\}

settings.name_in_paper: Online change-point detection for high-dimensional GLMs
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Statistical change-point detection guarantee (false alarm / detection probability), not a bandit regret problem
unmapped: Data with i.i.d. prices from the experiment set; test for at most one change-point in s-sparse GLM parameter
settings.definition_quote: we declare non-stationarity in the data $\{y_t,z_t,p_t\}_{t=1}^n$ if $\max_{t=m,m+1,\cdots,n-m} \mathcal{D}(t,n) >\gamma$.

conditions: Assumption 1: bounded covariates, ||theta_t||_1 <= C_theta, s-sparse, psi infinitely differentiable with psi''>0, unique optimal price in [p_l,p_u]
Assumption 2: covariates i.i.d. within segments, min eigenvalue >= sigma_l, (2+delta)-moment bound
tuning: c_lambda, c_gamma, c_m sufficiently large absolute constants

source.label: thm:regret
source.quote: Let $\pi$ be the CPDP algorithm with $m=c_ms\log(Td)$, $\lambda=c_{\lambda}\sqrt{\log(Td)}$, and $\gamma=c_{\gamma}s\lambda^2$, where $c_{\lambda}, c_{\gamma}, c_m > 0$ are absolute constants. Under Assumptions~\ref{assum_model} and \ref{assum_moment}, it holds that $R_T^\pi(\bm \theta_T)\leq C \sqrt{\Upsilon_TT}\left(\kappa_{\min}^{-2}\vee {s\log (Td)}\right)$, for any $\bm\theta_T$ that satisfies \Cref{ass_spacing}, where $C > 0$ is an absolute constant.

results.notes: Regret defined via expected revenue against per-round clairvoyant optimal price under piecewise-stationary parameters; recorded as dynamic regret. Absolute constant C hidden, so O notation. Setting mapping to continuum_other is approximate.

conditions: Assumption 4: pseudo-true mixture parameter in interior of Theta and within C_M ||theta_{tau_k}-theta_{tau_{k+1}}||_1 of both pre- and post-change parameters

source.label: cor_regret
source.quote: In addition to all the conditions in \Cref{thm:regret}, suppose that Assumption  \ref{assum:mixture} also holds, we have that $R_T^\pi(\bm \theta_T)\leq C s\sqrt{\Upsilon_T T}\log (Td)$, where $C>0$ is an absolute constant.

results.notes: Independent of change size kappa_min. Still requires SNR Assumption 3.

conditions: Instances satisfy Assumptions 1, 2 and 3 with exactly Upsilon_T change-points
Hard instances: linear Gaussian demand y_t = alpha_t + beta_t p_t + N(0,1) noise

source.label: thm:lowerbound
source.quote: Let $\mathcal{P}_T$ be the collection of distributions satisfying Assumptions \ref{assum_model}, \ref{assum_moment} and \ref{ass_spacing}, with the corresponding $\bm\theta_T$ possessing~$\Upsilon_T$ number of change-points, we have that $\inf_{\pi \in \Pi} \sup_{P(\bm\theta_T) \in \mathcal{P}_T} R_T^{\pi}(\bm\theta_T) \geq C\sqrt{T\Upsilon_T}/\log(\Upsilon_T)$, where $C>0$ is an absolute constant.

results.notes: Paper remarks that without the SNR assumption the bound improves to C sqrt(T Upsilon_T). Does not involve sparsity s.

source.label: prop:cp
source.quote: (i) If there is no change-point in $\{1, \ldots, n\}$, then $\mathbb{P}\left(\mbox{no change-point is detected} \right) =\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{T}_n = 0) ... \geq 1 - 3T^{-3}$.

bound.regime: single change-point tau with min(tau, n-tau) kappa^2 > c_snr s log(Td)

conditions: min(tau, n-tau) kappa^2 > c_snr s log(Td)

source.label: prop:cp
source.quote: (ii) If there exists a single change-point $\tau \in \{m, \ldots, n-m\}$, assuming that $\min(\tau,n-\tau)\kappa^2>c_{\mathrm{snr}}s\log(Td)$ ... it holds that $\mathbb{P}\left(\mathcal{T}_n=1 \right) \geq \mathbb {P} \left(\mathcal{D}(\tau,n)>\gamma \right)  \geq 1 - 3T^{-4}$.

results.notes: Missed-detection probability bound; implies detection delay O(s log(Td)/kappa^2) w.h.p.
